sections.overview: Uromys emmae is a giant rat in the family Muridae, known from Owi Island in Papua Province, Indonesia.
sections.identification: Its formal description rests on one museum specimen, so field identification has not been documented.
sections.habitat: The IUCN account presumes tropical moist forest, while noting that the species’ natural history is unknown.
sections.diet: No diet has been recorded for this species.
sections.behavior: Its behavior is unknown because no natural-history observations are available in the assessment.
sections.reproduction: No reproductive biology has been recorded.
sections.ecology: The Australian Museum review records one holotype from Owi Island and notes no later report of the species.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists it as Critically Endangered, Possibly Extinct, citing its tiny range, continuing habitat decline and failed searches.
